4) Egress controls: we need an explicit list of endpoints that Redwood Private would call out (if any) during normal operation and during upgrades. If you can provide a short table of outbound IP ranges / FQDNs and ports, that helps our netsec team move faster.

Marissa / team / Jenna 

Thanks  below are the high-level answers to Acme's asks. I'll bring more detail and sample firewall rules to the deep dive Monday.

1) Outbound endpoints & ports (normal operation)
- Control plane: optional (customer choice)  if enabled, control plane comms are outbound over TLS to api-control.redwood.ai on ports 443 only. IP ranges: 34.201.0.0/16, 34.202.0.0/16 (we will provide a signed list ahead of the pilot).
- Model registry & upgrades: if using our managed image registry, hosts registry.redwood.ai on 443; upgrades can be run manually by customer in air-gapped mode (we provide OCI images and checksums).
- Telemetry: optional; can be disabled. If enabled telemetry endpoints are telemetry.redwood.ai:443.

2) Egress / air-gapped modes
- Fully private VPC (no internet egress): supported. In this mode the customer is responsible for image distribution and control-plane interactions; we provide an on-prem package and signed OCI artifacts for manual install.
- Air-gapped upgrades: supported via offline image import + manual activation. We provide upgrade checklist and signed manifests.

3) Logging & retention
- We separate application-level request logs from infra logs. Current product supports configurable retention at the deployment-level for request logs (TTL in days); we can set long retention (7 years) for audit logs using customer-managed S3/GCS with lifecycle rules. Infra logs are by default 90 days but can be exported to customer storage for long-term retention.

4) PII handling / KV cache
- Field-level PII redaction: we provide a redaction hook that runs pre-persistence (open API hook) that can remove or hash specified fields before they hit KV or logs.
- Embeddings: embeddings generation can be disabled per-model or per-route; we also support a 'no-persist' mode for debug/pseudonymized datasets.

Attachments included for deep dive: sample firewall rules (text), airgap-upgrade-checklist.pdf, OCI image manifest example (sha256). I'll attach the short matrix and firewall snippets in the calendar invite.

Availability: I can join Mon 12/14 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
